cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has just finished speaking to all Israel. They're about to cross the Jordan River into the land God promised them. Then Moses tells them he's a hundred and twenty years old, and he's no longer able to come and go like he used to.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD told him he'd lead Israel across the Jordan himself.

cards.text: But Moses is NOT leaving them hanging. He says the LORD their God Himself will cross over ahead of them, destroy these nations before them, and they'll take the land from them.

cards.question: Besides the LORD, Moses names a man who will cross ahead of the people, just as the LORD said. Who is it?

cards.text: Moses reminds them the LORD will do to these nations what He did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, when He destroyed them and their land. That's your boss pulling up LAST year's record numbers right before the big meeting!

cards.question: Moses says once the LORD hands these nations over, Israel can deal with them however they like.
Moses tells the people to be strong and courageous and not to be afraid of these nations. What reason does he give them?

answers.text: The LORD their God goes with them
Joshua has never lost a battle
The nations are already running away

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will stay with them through the first battle, and after that they're on their own.

cards.text: Then Moses calls for Joshua, his assistant, and with ALL Israel watching, tells him what he told the people: be strong and courageous. The whole nation staring at you, friend, so no pressure, Joshua!

cards.question: Moses tells Joshua he'll go with the people into the land the LORD swore to their fathers, and he'll give it to them as their ___.
Moses tells Joshua that the LORD Himself goes before him and will be with him.

cards.text: So Moses writes down this law, and he does NOT toss it in a junk drawer. Trust me, friend, I know exactly where things go to get forgotten.

cards.question: Who does Moses hand the written law to?

answers.text: The priests and the elders of Israel

cards.text: Then Moses sets up a schedule. At the end of every seven years, during the Feast of Tabernacles, there's a gathering before the LORD at the place He will choose.

cards.question: At that gathering every seven years at the Feast of Tabernacles, what does Moses say is to be done?

answers.text: Count the people tribe by tribe
Choose a new leader for Israel

cards.question: Moses says to gather the people for that reading of the law. Who's supposed to be there?

answers.text: Only the men of each tribe
Only the priests and the elders

cards.question: Moses wants them all to listen and learn to ___ the LORD their God and carefully follow all the words of this law.
Moses says the children who don't know the law yet should wait until they're grown to hear it.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses the time of his death is near. He tells him to bring Joshua to the Tent of Meeting, and the two of them go.

cards.question: The LORD wants Moses and Joshua at the Tent of Meeting so that He can ___ Joshua.

cards.text: Then the LORD appears at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the cloud stands right over the entrance.
The LORD tells Moses he'll soon rest with his fathers. Then He tells Moses what the people will do in the land they're entering.

cards.question: What does the LORD say the people will do in the land they're entering?

answers.text: Turn to foreign gods and break His covenant
Stay faithful to Him for good
Refuse to go in and turn back

cards.text: On that day, the LORD says, His anger will burn against them, and He will abandon them and hide His face from them. Many troubles and afflictions will come on them.

cards.question: When those disasters come, what does the LORD say the people will ask?

answers.text: If it's because their God isn't with them
Why Moses ever left them behind
If Joshua led them the wrong way

cards.question: The LORD says He will hide His face because of all the evil they've done by turning to other gods.

cards.text: So the LORD gives Moses a job: write down a song, teach it to the Israelites and have them recite it. Not a speech, friend, a SONG!

cards.question: What does the LORD say this song is for?

answers.text: To be a witness for Him against them
To honor Moses after he dies

cards.text: The LORD says once He brings them into the land flowing with milk and honey, they'll eat their fill and prosper. Then they'll turn to other gods, reject Him and break His covenant.

cards.question: The LORD says this song will fade away after one generation.
The LORD talks about what the people are inclined to do. What does He say about it?

answers.text: He knows it before they enter the land
He'll learn it once they settle in
He'll see it after Moses dies

cards.text: That very day, Moses writes the song down and teaches it to the Israelites. THAT DAY, friend, and me, I'd have hit snooze on that reminder four times!
Then it's Joshua's big moment. The LORD commissions Joshua son of Nun.

cards.question: When the LORD commissions Joshua, He tells him the same thing Moses told him: be strong and courageous.
The LORD tells Joshua he'll bring the Israelites into the land. What does the LORD promise him?

answers.text: That He will be with him
That Moses will come back to help
That no one will fight against him

cards.text: Moses finishes writing the words of this law in a book, from beginning to end. Then he gives a command to the Levites who carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

cards.question: Where does Moses tell the Levites to put the Book of the Law?

answers.text: Beside the ark of the covenant
At the gate of the camp

cards.question: Moses says the Book of the Law is to stay there as a ___ against the people.

cards.text: Moses does NOT sugarcoat it: he knows how rebellious and stiff-necked they are. If they're already rebelling against the LORD while he's still alive, what about after he dies?

cards.question: Moses says that after he dies, the people will rebel less.
Moses has more words to speak. Who does he ask to be gathered before him to hear them?

answers.text: The elders and officers of the tribes
The kings of the nearby nations

cards.question: Moses says he'll call ___ and ___ to witness against them.
Moses looks ahead to the days after his death. What does he say will happen to the people?

answers.text: Peace because they keep the law

cards.text: We'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story is still going.

findings.problem: The card calls Joshua 'his assistant.' That fact comes from outside the passage (for example Exodus 24:13 or Numbers 11:28), but the card cites only Deuteronomy 31:7 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke 'The whole nation staring at you, friend, so no pressure, Joshua!' talks to the baker ('you, friend') and then to Joshua in the same breath. It reads as if the baker is the one being stared at, so the line doesn't land right away.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the men of each tribe', 'Only the priests and the elders'). The right answer, 'Everyone even the foreigners', is the only one that doesn't, so it stands out. Without its comma it also reads awkwardly.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The only attempt at humor in Stop 2 is 'Not a speech, friend, a SONG!' That is emphasis, not a joke. Moses being handed a song to teach a whole nation could hold a real laugh without muddying any fact.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Story card 8 sets up the question with 'If they're already rebelling against the LORD while he's still alive, what about after he dies?' That framing already rules out 'the people will rebel less,' so the true or false on card 9 is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'angels' and 'seas' match 'heaven' and 'earth' as parts of creation, but 'Joshua' is a person. That makes it a different kind of thing from the others.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, which the docs allow when the last verse is asked on a choice card. It tells no verse, yet it cites Deuteronomy 31:29, the same verse choice card 12 already cites.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verses? The last verse of the passage, or something else? The output format requires a verses value, and the citation rule only covers verses a card tells.
